text:
Dear Mr. Abernathy,

I write further to your letter of 3 September concerning the noise generated by our night-time deliveries to the Harbour Road depot. Please accept my apologies that this has disturbed you and your neighbors. We have reviewed our schedule and concluded that deliveries to the loading bay can be [1] to the hours between 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. from the first of next month.

[2] The change will, however, inevitably bring some additional vehicles onto the road during the day, which may cause some [3] to residents who commute at those times. We would be grateful if you would [4] us know whether you notice any difficulty, so that we may adjust the arrangements if necessary. We shall in any case review the new schedule formally in December.

Yours sincerely,
Corinna Hale
Site Manager

questions.explanation: Deliveries can be 'restricted to' certain hours, meaning limited to them. 'Restrained' is followed by 'from', 'resolved' needs a different construction, and 'relegated' implies demotion rather than a scheduling limit.

choices: We trust that this arrangement will resolve the problem described by the council and spare local residents further disturbance at night.
We regret that this arrangement will not resolve the problem you have described or spare your neighbors further disturbance at night.
We trust that this arrangement will have resolved the problem you have described before the first of next month.
We trust that this arrangement will resolve the problem you have described and spare your neighbors further disturbance at night.
questions.explanation: 'The change will, however, inevitably bring...' contrasts with a stated benefit, so the preceding sentence must express the hope that the problem raised in Mr. Abernathy's letter will be resolved. The reference to the council is unsupported, the sentence that says the problem will not be resolved leaves 'however' without a contrast, and 'will have resolved ... before the first of next month' contradicts the start date of the new hours.
Extra vehicles 'may cause some inconvenience to residents'. The other nouns cannot be 'caused to' residents in this meaning.
'Let us know' is the fixed expression meaning inform us; 'make us know', 'keep us know' and 'give us know' are not grammatical.

text:
Why Universities Are Rethinking Their Grading

A growing number of universities are replacing traditional percentage marks with broader grade bands, arguing that fine distinctions give a false impression of precision. Critics, [1], object that employers rely on detailed marks to identify the strongest candidates.

[2] A study of twelve institutions found that the difference between two students whose marks differed by a single point was statistically meaningless. Supporters also contend that narrower scales encourage students to [3] genuine understanding rather than the pursuit of marginal gains. Whether employers will have [4] to the change by the next recruitment round remains uncertain, since many recruitment systems still filter applicants by a numerical threshold.

At Hartwell University, which introduced five grade bands in 2022, the proportion of graduates placed in the top band fell from 38 percent to 24 percent, a shift the registrar attributes to stricter moderation rather than weaker cohorts.

questions.explanation: 'Critics, by contrast, object' sets the critics against the universities that are changing their marks. 'In short', 'for instance' and 'as a result' summarise, exemplify or conclude, and none marks opposition.

choices: The case for the reform rests largely on its popularity among students rather than on evidence about marks.
The case for the reform rests largely on evidence that small differences in marks reflect chance rather than ability.
The case for the reform is weakened by evidence that small differences in marks reflect ability rather than chance.
The case against the reform rests largely on evidence that small differences in marks reflect ability rather than chance.
questions.explanation: The next sentence cites a study showing that a one-point difference was 'statistically meaningless', and 'Supporters also contend' continues the case for reform, so the blank must announce evidence that small differences reflect chance. The 'case against' version and the 'weakened' version say the opposite of the study, and the 'popularity' version denies that evidence exists.

Narrower scales encourage students to 'prioritize' understanding, meaning give it greater importance than marginal gains. 'Patronize' means treat condescendingly, 'publicize' means advertise and 'polarize' means divide, none of which suits 'genuine understanding'.

After 'will have' the past participle 'adapted' forms the future perfect, as in 'will have adapted to the change'. The base form, the '-ing' form and the noun 'adaptation' cannot complete that verb phrase.

text:
To: All Employees
From: Marta Szymanski, Facilities Director
Subject: Transition to hot-desking

From 3 March, the third and fourth floors will operate on a hot-desking basis. Employees who work in the office fewer than three days a week will no longer be assigned a permanent desk and will instead reserve a workstation through the booking application. [1] Personal belongings must be stored in the lockers provided, since desks will be cleared nightly.

The change is intended to [2] the use of floor space, which on average is occupied at barely half its capacity. [3] some staff may initially find the arrangement unsettling, the experience of other companies suggests that satisfaction rises once teams adapt. Team leaders will [4] a rota to ensure that colleagues who collaborate closely are seated together on the days they attend.

Demonstration sessions will be held in the third-floor canteen at noon on 24 and 26 February. Anyone unable to attend may request a locker allocation and a short training video through the Facilities helpdesk before 28 February.

choices: Bookings may be made up to two weeks ahead, and desks left unclaimed by nine will be reassigned permanently to other colleagues.
Bookings may be made up to two weeks ahead, and desks left unclaimed by nine will be released for use by other colleagues.
Bookings may be made up to two weeks ahead, and desks left unclaimed by nine will be released to their previous occupants.
Bookings may be made up to two weeks ahead, and desks left unclaimed by nine will remain closed to other colleagues.
questions.explanation: A system meant to raise occupancy from 'barely half' of capacity must free unused desks for others, which is what releasing unclaimed desks to other colleagues does. Reassigning them permanently contradicts 'no longer be assigned a permanent desk', the previous occupants no longer have assigned desks, and keeping desks closed would defeat the purpose of the change.

To 'optimize' the use of floor space is to make the best of it, which matches the stated problem of rooms occupied at half capacity; 'originate', 'outsource' and 'outweigh' make no sense with 'use of floor space'.

'Although some staff may initially find the arrangement unsettling' concedes a drawback before the positive claim about rising satisfaction. 'Because' and 'unless' set up a cause or a condition that the sentence does not support, and 'whether' would need 'or not'.
Team leaders will 'draw up' a rota, meaning prepare it in writing; 'draw on' means make use of, 'draw out' means prolong, and 'draw back' means retreat.

text:
URGENT PRODUCT RECALL
Brightwell Home Appliances

Brightwell has identified a fault in the thermostat of its Model T-40 electric kettle, manufactured between January and June last year. [1] In rare cases, this may prevent the kettle from switching itself off after the water has boiled, which could result in overheating. Affected kettles carry a batch number beginning with BK, printed on the underside of the base.

Owners are advised to stop using the kettle immediately and to [2] the product to the retailer from which it was bought, or to contact our customer service team on 0800 555 0142. A replacement or full refund will be provided [3] proof of purchase. [4] no injuries have been reported to date, we are taking this action as a precaution. Kettles from other production runs and other Brightwell models are not affected. We apologize for any inconvenience.

choices: Before dispatch, the contacts inside the thermostat were tested by an independent laboratory in Leeds.
Over time, the plastic casing around the thermostat may become discolored by repeated exposure to heat.
Retailers that stocked the kettle before July have been asked to remove all remaining units from sale.
Over time, the contacts inside the thermostat may become fused together and no longer respond to heat.
questions.explanation: The following sentence begins 'In rare cases, this may prevent the kettle from switching itself off', so 'this' needs an antecedent that could cause that failure; thermostat contacts fused together and unresponsive to heat do. Discoloration of the casing is harmless, an earlier laboratory test and the withdrawal of units from sale cannot be what 'this' refers to.

Owners are told to stop using the kettle and 'return' it to the retailer. 'Retain' means keep, 'relocate' means move to another place, and 'reclaim' means take back for oneself, none of which suits sending a recalled product back.
A refund is given 'on presentation of' proof of purchase, meaning when it is shown. 'In pursuit of' means chasing, 'in excess of' means above, and 'on behalf of' means representing someone.

'Although no injuries have been reported' concedes the absence of harm before stating that action is being taken anyway. 'Unless' sets a condition, 'now that' would make the lack of injuries the reason for acting, and 'insofar as' limits the extent of something.

text:
Hartley & Moss Chartered Accountants

Running a growing business leaves little time for tax planning, yet decisions taken early in a company's life can [1] its liabilities for years to come. Hartley & Moss has advised owner-managed firms for more than three decades, and our partners combine technical expertise with a practical understanding of commercial pressures. Our services include corporate tax planning, VAT advice, payroll and the preparation of annual accounts.

[2] We do not offer generic packages; instead, each client is assigned a partner who becomes familiar with the business and anticipates problems before they arise. [3] you are preparing for a sale, a succession or a period of rapid expansion, we shall tailor our advice accordingly. Contact us before 31 March to arrange a complimentary review, [4] which we shall outline the savings that may be available to you.

Our offices in Leeds and York are open from Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5.30 p.m.

questions.explanation: Early decisions can 'dictate' a company's liabilities, meaning they largely determine them for years to come. 'Indicate' means to point to, 'vindicate' means to prove right, and 'dedicate' means to devote, so none of them expresses that causal control.

choices: Our fees are deliberately modest, which is why many of our clients have remained with us for over twenty years.
Our approach is deliberately personal, which is why many of our clients have remained with us for over twenty years.
Our approach has been deliberately personal, which is why few of our clients have remained with us for over twenty years.
Our approach is deliberately standardized, which is why many of our clients have remained with us for over twenty years.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says 'We do not offer generic packages; instead, each client is assigned a partner', which develops the idea of a personal approach. A 'standardized' approach is the very thing rejected there, a statement about low fees does not lead into it, and 'few of our clients have remained' contradicts the claim of lasting loyalty.

'Whether you are preparing for a sale, a succession or a period of rapid expansion' introduces a list of alternatives, all of which receive the same tailored advice. 'Although', 'because' and 'unless' cannot present alternatives joined by 'or'.

'A complimentary review, at which we shall outline the savings' uses 'at which' to refer back to the review as the occasion of the explanation. 'To which', 'of which' and 'for which' cannot link a review to what happens during it.

text:
Annual Conference of the Regional Planning Association
Program Notes for Delegates

Registration will open at 8.30 a.m. on Thursday, [1] the opening plenary will not begin until 9.30. Parallel sessions will follow at 11.00, and delegates are asked to indicate their choices on the form provided so that rooms of appropriate size can be allocated.

[2] Sessions on housing and transport are expected to attract the largest audiences, and places will therefore be offered on a first-come basis. Lunch will be served between 1.00 and 2.00 p.m.; delegates with dietary requirements should [3] the organizers in advance. The conference dinner, [4] will take place at the Guildhall, requires a separate booking. Tickets cost £45 and must be purchased by the Friday of the previous week. Shuttle buses will leave the main hotel at 6.30 p.m.

questions.explanation: 'Whereas' sets the early opening of registration against the later start of the plenary. 'In case', 'provided that' and 'so that' would make the plenary conditional on, or a purpose of, registration, which the schedule does not say.

choices: Late forms will be accepted without any restriction, so delegates may submit their choices on the day itself.
Some sessions are likely to be oversubscribed, so delegates are advised to return their forms as late as possible.
All sessions are likely to be undersubscribed, so delegates are advised to return their forms as early as possible.
Some sessions are likely to be oversubscribed, so delegates are advised to return their forms as early as possible.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says that housing and transport sessions will be popular and that places go 'on a first-come basis', so advising delegates to return forms early is the logical lead-in. Advice to return forms late, a forecast of undersubscription, and an unrestricted late-form policy all contradict the first-come rule.

Delegates with special diets should 'notify' (inform) the organizers in advance. 'Assure' and 'reassure' would mean giving the organizers a guarantee or comfort, and 'oblige' does not take this meaning.

'The conference dinner, which will take place at the Guildhall' is a non-defining clause set off by commas, and it needs 'which' for a thing. 'That' cannot follow a comma in this type of clause, 'what' cannot refer back to a noun, and 'whom' refers to people.

text:
Isabel Moreno [10:02]: Have the auditors replied about the revised schedule?
Gareth Pugh [10:05]: They have. They can begin on Tuesday the 14th, [1] they would need access to the accounts ledger by the preceding Friday, and they have asked for the inventory records to be available on the first day.
Isabel Moreno [10:06]: That is feasible. [2]
Gareth Pugh [10:08]: Agreed. I'll also ask whether they would [3] a joint session with the tax team on the first morning; the conference room on the third floor is free until noon.
Isabel Moreno [10:09]: Good idea. Please make sure they understand that the migration to the new system is still [4] to be completed by the 10th. Once it is finished, Dario will email them the login details so that nothing is held up.
Gareth Pugh [10:11]: Understood. I'll write to them this afternoon and copy you in.

questions.explanation: 'Provided that' states the condition on which they can start on the 14th: access to the ledger by the preceding Friday. 'Even if', 'as though' and 'whereas' do not make the access a condition.

choices: However, the migration of the ledger will have to be finished before then, otherwise the data may be incomplete.
Therefore, the migration of the ledger is finished, otherwise the auditors would have no data to examine.
However, the migration of the ledger will have to be postponed until then, otherwise the data may be incomplete.
However, the migration of the ledger has been finished since then, so the data may be incomplete.
questions.explanation: Access is needed 'by the preceding Friday' and the migration is 'still ... to be completed by the 10th', so the message must say the migration has to be finished before the auditors need the ledger. A migration 'postponed until then' would not meet the deadline, 'has been finished since then' contradicts 'still', and 'is finished' also contradicts 'still to be completed'.
A schedule can 'accommodate' a joint session, meaning make room for it. 'Accumulate' means gather, 'accompany' means go with, and 'acquaint' means make familiar with.
'Is still scheduled to be completed' needs the past participle after 'is'. 'Scheduling', 'schedule' and 'schedules' do not form a passive construction here.

text:
Statement of Account – Harcourt Industrial Supplies

Customer: Brandt Engineering Ltd
Period: 1 April to 30 June

The total below reflects all goods supplied during the period (£18,420.50) and credit notes issued up to 30 June (£1,315.00), leaving a balance of £17,105.50. [1] Items returned after that date will be credited on the next statement. The balance is payable within thirty days of the statement date; amounts outstanding beyond that period will [2] interest at 2 percent per month.

We would draw your attention to the following. [3] the volume discount agreed in January, invoice 20871 has been issued at the standard rate, and a credit note for £460.00 will follow. Should you disagree with any entry, please notify us in writing [4] fourteen days of receipt, quoting the invoice number and your purchase order reference.

choices: Credit notes issued after 30 June are not included in this statement and will appear on the next one.
Goods supplied after 30 June are not included in this statement and will be credited on the next one.
Credit notes issued after 30 June have been included in this statement, as the balance below shows.
Credit notes issued before 30 June are not included in this statement and will be shown separately.
questions.explanation: The following sentence refers to 'that date' and to the 'next statement', so the gap must name 30 June and say that later items are postponed: 'Credit notes issued after 30 June are not included ... and will appear on the next one'. Credit notes issued before 30 June contradict the opening sentence, 'have been included' contradicts the cut-off, and goods cannot be 'credited'.

Overdue amounts 'accrue interest', meaning interest builds up on them. 'Accrete' means grow by accumulation of matter, 'accede' means agree and 'accuse' means blame, so none takes 'interest' as an object.

'Contrary to the volume discount agreed in January' signals that the invoice departs from the agreement and needs a correction. 'Pursuant to' would mean in accordance with it, and 'owing to' and 'thanks to' would make the discount the cause of the standard rate.
'Within fourteen days of receipt' sets a time limit measured from the moment of receipt. 'During' and 'since' do not express a deadline, and 'by' would need a date or time point, not a period.

text:
Dear Ms. Karlsson,

I am delighted to confirm that the Board of Trustees has approved your nomination as a member of the Advisory Council of the Linden Arts Foundation. The Council meets four times a year, and members are expected to attend at least three meetings annually. [1] Your term will run for three years, after which you will be eligible for reappointment for a second term.

Your first meeting will take place on 14 October at the Foundation's offices on Linden Row, where a short induction for new members will precede the formal agenda. Although the position is unremunerated, the Foundation will [2] reasonable travel expenses on production of receipts. [3] a member is unable to attend a meeting, apologies should be sent to the secretary at least forty-eight hours beforehand. Members are also asked to declare any interest that might [4] with their duties.

Yours sincerely,
Olivier Bastien
Chair of Trustees

choices: Appointments to the Council are made for life, so that its membership remains stable over many years.
Appointments to the Council will be made next spring, once the Trustees have agreed the new rules.
Nominations to the Council are made by the public each spring, so that it is widely representative.
Appointments to the Council are made for a fixed period, so that its membership is regularly renewed.
questions.explanation: The following sentence speaks of 'Your term' lasting three years with possible reappointment, which presupposes fixed-period appointments. Appointments for life contradict this, appointments 'next spring' contradict the Board's approval already announced, and public nominations contradict the Board's role.
A foundation 'reimburses' travel expenses, meaning it repays them on production of receipts; 'reinforce', 'reinstate' and 'reiterate' do not take 'expenses' sensibly.

'In the event that a member is unable to attend' introduces a possible situation and the action to take. 'On the grounds that' would give a reason, 'on condition that' would state a requirement, and 'in the hope that' expresses a wish, none of which suits an inability to attend.
An interest that might 'conflict with' a member's duties is the fixed collocation; 'confront' takes a direct object without 'with', 'confine' means restrict, and 'confess' means admit.

text:
Retailers Wrestle With the Cost of Returns

Online retailers are discovering that the convenience they offer customers has a price. Around a fifth of goods bought on the internet are returned, [1] the proportion in physical stores is closer to one in twenty. The expense of collecting, inspecting and restocking these items now weighs heavily on margins.

[2] Several fashion chains have begun to charge customers for returns, a step that was unthinkable only two years ago. Others are experimenting with so-called returnless refunds, [3] shoppers are allowed to keep low-value items rather than send them back. Analysts caution that the strategy may prove [4] if it encourages customers to order more than they intend to keep, thereby inflating the very costs it is meant to reduce.

A study by the Lindqvist Retail Institute puts the average cost of processing a single return at between eight and fifteen euros, a sum that can exceed the profit on a low-priced garment.

questions.explanation: 'Whereas the proportion in physical stores is closer to one in twenty' contrasts online returns with store returns. 'Since' would make store returns the cause of online returns, 'unless' sets a condition, and 'lest' expresses fear of an outcome.

choices: The financial pressure has encouraged companies to extend policies that, until recently, were treated as a competitive disadvantage.
The financial pressure has forced companies to reconsider policies that, until recently, were treated as a competitive advantage.
The financial pressure has forced customers to reconsider policies that, until recently, were treated as a company secret.
The financial pressure had forced companies to reconsider policies that, until recently, were treated as a competitive advantage.
questions.explanation: 'The financial pressure' picks up 'weighs heavily on margins' and prepares the reversal described next, where chains 'have begun to charge customers for returns'. Extending a policy seen as a 'disadvantage' would not lead to charging, customers are not the ones under financial pressure, and 'had forced' clashes with the present perfect 'have begun'.

'Whereby shoppers are allowed to keep low-value items' defines how the refund scheme works (by which). 'Whereupon' means after which, 'whereof' means of which, and 'wherefore' means for which reason, none of which fits.

A scheme that inflates 'the very costs it is meant to reduce' defeats its own purpose, which is 'counterproductive'. 'Counterintuitive' describes something surprising, 'counterbalanced' means offset, and 'counteractive' means working against another thing.
